title: Holding Resort Club Memberships at Several Ashbury Resorts
content:
A person may hold Resort Club Memberships at more than one Ashbury resort. Each membership is a separate contract with its own dues, passes and benefits. No limit is set on the number of resorts at which one person may hold a membership; the limit that applies within a single resort is the club's rule of one membership per resort.

## Points of judgement

**Does a second resort's membership change the first one?** No. Each membership is its own contract: its dues are invoiced on its own account, its guest passes are its own, and its benefits follow its own level.

**Is there a ceiling on how many resorts?** No ceiling is set across resorts.

**What does the limit within a resort turn on?** It is the separate per-resort rule of Resort Club Memberships: at a given resort's club a person holds at most one membership, whatever its level.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A member who holds a Spa Club Membership at one resort applies for a Beach & Pool Club Membership at a different Ashbury resort. Holding the first membership is no bar to the second, because the two are at different resorts; once opened, the second membership carries its own dues, its own guest passes and its own benefits.
